mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero drift baseline (p > 0.05) during confirmed high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: During labor market tightening episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) after controlling for inflation and risk sentiment proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In expansionary demand regimes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the observed INDPRO acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests the Federal Reserve is likely to hold rates steady, reducing discount rate expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During deflationary periods, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when other risk factors are controlled for.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) falls by more than 10% from the prior month, it indicates cooling credit demand, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as risk aversion rises.
failure_condition: In credit market cooling episodes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after adjusting for macroeconomic risk proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in weekly job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 500,000 followed by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% simultaneously signals a strong labor market, which can drive S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 500,000 and UNRATE < 3.5% in the same week
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when controlling for sector-specific earnings momentum and global risk sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 4% suggests demand is outpacing supply without a strong wage growth offset, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: During moderate demand expansion phases, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when accounting for forward guidance and earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the ratio of new home sales (not available in the provided catalog) cannot be used; instead, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110 (as of the latest available) for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 110 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In supply-constrained environments, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the contraction in INDPRO.
